pool.text: Both the Lenape and the Miami Nation relinquished tribal lands in central Indiana.
Indianapolis was established as a planned city for the new seat of government.
The Indianapolis City Market was founded as the city's public market building.
Growth occurred with the opening of the National Road through town.
A small segment of the failed Indiana Central Canal was opened.
Indianapolis was one of the hardest hit cities in a major flood.
The Madam Walker Legacy Center opened in the African-American neighborhood.
Hinkle opened as the world's largest basketball arena with fifteen thousand seats.
The City-County Building became the first high-rise to surpass the monument height.
The twin Riley Towers residential buildings were completed in Indianapolis.
The Indiana Pacers were founded and began playing in the American Basketball Association.
Unigov expanded the city land area and increased its population.
Indianapolis established a consolidated city-county form of government under the Unigov provision.
The Indianapolis Colts of the National Football League relocated to the city from Baltimore.
The Salesforce Tower was completed as the city tallest building.
Victory Field replaced Bush Stadium as the home venue for the Indians.
Gainbridge Fieldhouse opened and replaced Market Square Arena as home for the Fever and Pacers.
Two large capital projects including Lucas Oil Stadium were completed.
The Indianapolis metropolitan area had the highest concentration of chain restaurants per capita.
A mass shooting occurred at a FedEx facility on the southwest side.
